clue.text: Subscribe a pound? That's notable

parts.note: to subscribe is to sign your name
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether pledging a pound to a cause is worth remarking on.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal success is a striking, remarkable one, so the adjective matches notable.

clue.text: Wise behaviour, having extended account with financial centre

parts.note: a saga is a long story
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Sensible conduct over a long tale about the banking district.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacity is shrewd judgement, the quality of acting with wisdom.

clue.text: London theatre supported by left-winger to go on world tour

indicators.note: in a down answer the first word stands on top of the second

parts.note: the Globe is Shakespeare's theatre on London's South Bank
TROT is short for Trotskyist, a far-left activist

explanation.surface: A theatre backed by a socialist heads off travelling internationally.
explanation.definitionFit: To globetrot is to travel widely around the planet as a tourist.

clue.text: A way to be mounted on horse

parts.note: a stride is a way of walking, a gait

explanation.surface: A method for getting onto a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Astride means with legs either side, as a rider sits in the saddle.

clue.text: Shows moving state of affairs, briefly, about employment

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around, about, the word for employment

parts.note: CIRCS is a colloquial shortening of circumstances, the state of affairs
employment of something is its use

explanation.surface: Performances shift with the shorthand situation regarding jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' belongs with the definition: these are travelling shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Circuses are touring entertainments that travel from town to town with their big tops.

clue.text: Risk about article leading to bitterness about this volume

indicators.note: the risk word wraps around the article

parts.note: to imperil is to put at risk
A is the indefinite article
gall is bitterness or resentment
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Hazard related to an item leads to resentment over this amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' appears twice: first as a wrapping signal, then as the word ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperial gallon is the British measure of liquid capacity, about 4.5 litres.

clue.text: Boasted over share in profit — it helps to keep a cool head

definitions.text: it helps to keep a cool head

indicators.note: in a down answer the first part is placed over the second

parts.note: crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast
a cut is one's portion of the takings

explanation.surface: A braggart takes a slice of the gains, which keeps him calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool head' suggests calmness, but it means a head kept literally cool by short hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short haircut, leaving the scalp airy.

clue.text: Birds to shoot — precisely

definitions.meaning: wading birds; the plural is the same as the singular
to fire accurately from a hidden spot

explanation.definitionFit: The marsh bird gave its name to shooting from cover, as sniping at snipe needed marksmanship.

clue.text: Spies can be facilitators of people's aims

definitions.meaning: the ... on a gun help the shooter aim

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spies' looks like a noun for secret agents but is a verb, catches sight of.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means notices; as a noun the aiming devices on a firearm.

clue.text: The interruption that's stupid, eliminating one way to reverse course

indicators.note: something stupid is muddled, so the letters are jumbled
the named letter is removed from the jumbled letter pool

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A daft interjection is dropped by someone changing direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of THE INTERRUPTION, remove one I, and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-point turn is the driving manoeuvre for turning a car round in a narrow road.

clue.text: One of the spirits available from good innkeeper

parts.note: a host keeps an inn or entertains guests

explanation.surface: A spirit, as in a drink, served by a decent landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests spirits as drinks at a pub; the definition means a phantom.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is a disembodied spectre, one kind of supernatural being.

clue.text: With leaders away, chap opening event

indicators.note: the leading letter of each of the two words is dropped

explanation.surface: A man speaking first at an occasion, minus the bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop C from chap and O from opening, leaving HAP and PENING.
explanation.definitionFit: A happening is an occurrence or an organised improvised performance.

clue.text: Garment one's used in short science experiment, initially

parts.note: CHEM is short for chemistry
one is I, so one's is I'S

indicators.note: only the opening letter of experiment is used

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing gets used in a brief lab test.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemise is a loose shift or undergarment worn by women.

clue.text: Inside right container I loaded maximally

indicators.note: the letter I goes inside the combination of the other pieces

parts.note: a chest is a box for storing things

explanation.surface: I packed the right box to the very brim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' looks like filling the box, but it means wealthy here.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for wealthy, so most loaded is the superlative of rich.

clue.text: Weapons training that makes sailor understand routine, when in charge

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
to get something is to understand it

indicators.note: the routine word sits in the charge word

parts.note: a price is what is charged
an act is a performer's routine

explanation.surface: Drill that lets a seaman grasp the procedure while the officer is in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when in charge' looks like a phrase about authority; 'when' is a link and 'charge' is PRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Target practice is shooting at marks to improve a marksman's aim with guns.

clue.text: Quick movement, penning boy's first name

indicators.note: the swiftness word encloses, pens in, the other letter

parts.note: celerity is swiftness of motion

indicators.note: only the opening letter of boy's is used

explanation.surface: A fast move to write down a lad's given name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First name' looks like one phrase but splits: 'first' takes B, and 'name' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A big name is a famous person, so a celebrity is a household name.

clue.text: Stopped working after a king's held up

indicators.note: the resting word comes after the other pieces

parts.note: R is short for rex, king; the 's is 'has'
rested means stopped work for a time

explanation.surface: A monarch was delayed and so took a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrested development is development held back, so arrested can mean halted or delayed.

clue.text: Fatted calf, say, present for festive occasion

definitions.meaning: read literally, a calf being fattened is livestock (stock) being filled up
a small gift put into a Christmas stocking

explanation.walkthrough: The fatted calf of the prodigal son's feast is a stock animal being filled.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocking fillers are small Christmas gifts tucked into a hanging stocking.

clue.text: The ache that's tormented a noted sprinter

indicators.note: letters in torment are twisted into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A famous runner suffers a painful muscle strain.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, famous for short bursts of speed.

clue.text: Person making hostile takeover has driven frantically around area

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the area letter
a frantic state scrambles the letters

explanation.surface: A corporate raider has hurried wildly around a district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hostile takeover' suggests a company raid; here it means a military incursion.
explanation.definitionFit: An invader seizes territory by force, an aggressive capture of land.

clue.text: Place of worship, church primate left

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A church's leading bishop departs from the place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, which suits the church surface, but it is an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small church or a room set aside for prayer.

clue.text: What makes one stand, perhaps, for such a difficult situation

definitions.text: What makes one stand, perhaps, for such a difficult situation

parts.words: What makes one stand, perhaps, for such a difficult situation
parts.note: a seat too hot to sit on makes anyone leap up; the phrase also names an awkward position of responsibility

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a scalding chair would make you jump to your feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the hot seat means facing pressure or tough questioning in a tricky position.

clue.text: Gripping part of hobby expert alone comprehends

indicators.note: the phrase takes in, comprehends, the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: An enthusiast for a pastime understands it on his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hobby' means a pastime in the surface, but it is also a small falcon.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby is a small falcon, and a talon is a bird of prey's claw.

clue.text: Inclined to include verse making one's existence OK

indicators.note: the word for inclined takes the verse letter inside it

parts.note: liable means likely or inclined to do something

explanation.surface: Someone prone to poetry finds that it makes life bearable.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere livable is fit to live in, tolerable for day-to-day life.

clue.text: Party committee built poor reforms

indicators.note: the letters are formed again into a new shape

explanation.surface: A political committee overhauls a badly made structure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Politburo was the chief policy-making body of the Soviet Communist Party.

clue.text: Be powerless to resist current trend in meaning

definitions.meaning: to be carried along by a current
the ... of an argument is its general gist or tenor

explanation.definitionFit: The verb describes floating helplessly with water; the noun is the general sense of what someone says.

clue.text: Old-fashioned kind of record that keeps track of minutes

definitions.meaning: writing by hand, as against shorthand or typing
the ... of a clock shows the minutes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Minutes' suggests notes of a meeting, matching the record idea, but it is the clock's hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Handwriting in full, and the minute pointer on a clock face, share this name.

clue.text: Showing effects of strain in fight with editor

parts.note: a fray is a brawl or fight

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is worn out after a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Frayed nerves or tempers are worn down by stress, like a fabric's worn edges.
